    - heading "Understand Compass" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "A compass copies a radius. Opening 5 at one centre transfers r=5 to another centre. Changing the opening mid-copy makes an unequal circle. A useful rule is Copied radius: r_new=r_original. You can learn Compass by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: Set the opening to the source radius, move the spike to the new centre, and swing without changing the hinge. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
    - paragraph: "In real life, circle drawing: A compass draws equal-radius circles. Watch out: Changing compass width while copying. Keep the compass width fixed."
